forces.title: Electrification Reshaping Component Value Pool Towards EV Parts
forces.description: Rising EV adoption is fundamentally reshaping the auto component value pool. The shift is from traditional mechanical and engine-related components towards high-value EV components such as batteries, motors, power electronics, semiconductors, sensors, controllers, thermal management systems, and embedded software. EV electronics now constitute around 23% of the Bill of Materials (BOM) compared to less than 10% in ICE vehicles, creating significant opportunities for manufacturers of technology-intensive automotive components and driving strategic reorientation for the industry.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Government Policies Boosting Domestic Manufacturing and EV Value Chain
forces.description: Government initiatives like the PLI-Auto Scheme (attracting Rs 44,326 crore investments by FY26) and PM E-DRIVE (Rs 10,900 crore outlay) are accelerating domestic capacity creation and reducing import dependence for critical automotive technologies. The PLI-ACC Scheme for battery manufacturing (Rs 18,100 crore outlay) is also a key pillar in strengthening the domestic EV value chain. These policies encourage substantial investments across batteries, advanced electronics, and EV components, enhancing supply-chain resilience and fostering value addition within the industry.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Strengthening Global Supply Chain Integration and Export Opportunities
forces.description: India's auto component exports more than doubled from FY21 to FY26, projected to grow further by 8% in FY27, supported by supply-chain diversification, improving manufacturing capabilities, and cost competitiveness. Major global OEMs are increasingly making India a component sourcing hub. This strengthens India's position in the global automotive ecosystem, attracting foreign investment and increasing procurement from Indian subsidiaries, leading to robust export growth opportunities in diverse markets like North America and Asia, and enhancing India's share in the global automotive value chain.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Volatile Raw Material and Freight Costs Pressuring Profitability
forces.description: The auto ancillary industry faces significant pressure from volatility in raw materials (such as semiconductors, battery cells, rare earth minerals) and elevated freight costs, often exacerbated by geopolitical developments. While long-term customer relationships and contractual cost pass-through mechanisms with OEMs offer some earnings resilience, continued dependence on imported technology-intensive components remains a key monitorable. This necessitates strategic sourcing, localisation efforts, and diversified geographic exposure to mitigate potential profit margin erosion, particularly for export-oriented manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Evolving US Tariff Regime Poses Uncertainty for Export Manufacturers
forces.description: Evolving US tariff policies, including a 10% reciprocal tariff on certain products and an additional 25% tariff under the US Section 232 on covered auto components, remain a key monitorable. Despite the USA being India's largest export destination (~26% of auto component exports in FY26), these tariffs can pressure profitability, particularly for export-oriented manufacturers. The impact is expected to vary depending on product coverage, customer negotiations, and cost-sharing arrangements, favoring companies with specialized products, overseas manufacturing facilities, and diversified geographic exposure.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Industry Transitioning to Technology and Engineering-Oriented Ecosystem
forces.description: The Indian auto component industry is undergoing a structural transformation from a predominantly manufacturing-led sector towards a more technology and engineering-oriented ecosystem. Future growth is increasingly driven by higher content per vehicle, advanced electronics integration, and software-enabled systems. This includes components for ADAS, infotainment, connected vehicle technologies, sensors, controllers, and power electronics, shifting the industry's value pool from metal-intensive products to digital and software-driven solutions, requiring significant investments in advanced manufacturing capabilities and R&D.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Rising Component Content Per Vehicle Drives Value Addition
forces.description: The growing preference for SUVs and premium vehicles, coupled with stricter safety and emissions norms, is significantly increasing the component content per vehicle. This trend supports demand for higher-value systems and drives greater value addition within the auto ancillary industry. This, alongside healthy vehicle production and resilient aftermarket demand, is a principal growth driver, ensuring manufacturers can capture more revenue per unit produced across various vehicle segments, thereby contributing to overall industry growth and profitability.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Accelerated Investment in Digital and Software Foundations
forces.description: Geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility is not slowing transformation but accelerating it, pushing automotive companies to double down on digital and software foundations. This involves strengthening data capabilities, improving data flows, and increasing strategic independence. Tier 1 suppliers are focusing on analytics-driven and technology-led strategies to enhance speed and leverage across OEM relationships, ultimately turning complexity into a competitive advantage and driving innovation for diversified growth. This shift enables greater resilience and adaptability across the value chain by prioritizing core technological robustness.

forces.title: Continued Reliance on Imported Critical Components for Tech-Intensive Parts
forces.description: India's auto component industry faces continued dependence on certain critical components like semiconductors, battery cells, sensors, advanced electronics, and other technology-intensive parts, reflected in significant import growth from FY21 to FY26. This reliance makes the sector vulnerable to global supply chain disruptions, geopolitical volatility, and currency fluctuations. Strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities for these high-value components is crucial for achieving greater control over the value chain, ensuring a favorable trade balance, and enhancing long-term competitiveness and resilience against external shocks.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Tier 1 Suppliers Need Diversification Beyond OEM Roadmaps
forces.description: Tier 1 automotive suppliers are technical scale leaders in AI, data, and simulation but face the strategic challenge of reducing dependence on OEM roadmaps. Their innovation momentum is often throttled by OEM investment timing, creating a gap between their readiness for change and the structures dictating its implementation. Success requires redirecting technology scale toward diversified growth, potentially through targeted M&A for software/data capabilities and expanding into industrial, mobility services, and energy ecosystems, rather than solely following OEM investment cycles, to ensure sustained growth and profitability.

forces.title: Low R&D Spending Impedes Advanced Manufacturing & Innovation
forces.description: India lags its Asian peers in R&D spending, which is primarily concentrated in a few sectors and not yet a strategic priority for most corporates. This low investment limits advanced manufacturing capabilities, keeping the economy focused on low-to-mid-tech production. For the auto component industry, this hinders innovation, making it harder to compete with technology-driven exporters, including China and South Korea. To overcome this, greater private-sector participation, stronger innovation ecosystems, and improved research-to-commercialisation pipelines are essential for long-term global competitiveness.

forces.title: Accelerated EV Investments and Ecosystem Development
forces.description: The EV sector is witnessing substantial investments in capacity expansion and EV parts, with ICRA estimating Rs. 25,000-30,000 crore for FY26. Total investments in India's EV sector reached approximately Rs. 2.23 lakh crore between 2020-2025, alongside significant investment in public charging infrastructure. Global players like VinFast are setting up manufacturing facilities, and companies like Ola Electric are developing proprietary cell manufacturing. This influx of capital and strategic initiatives accelerates the growth of the EV component ecosystem, strengthening domestic capabilities and supply chains.

forces.title: Expanding Vehicle Parc Fueling Robust Aftermarket Component Demand
forces.description: The aftermarket segment for auto components is a significant stability provider, projected to grow at a 6-10% CAGR to US$ 16 billion by 2030. This growth is consistently supported by an expanding vehicle parc (total vehicles on road) and a rising average vehicle age, increasing demand for replacement parts and regular maintenance. This segment provides a consistent revenue stream, complementing OEM demand and mitigating cyclical risks associated with new vehicle sales, thereby driving overall industry resilience and contributing to stable profitability for component manufacturers and distributors.

forces.title: Geopolitical Uncertainty Accelerating De-risking Through Technology Adoption
forces.description: Rather than derailing technological progress, geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility is accelerating it. Companies are not pausing investments but are doubling down on digital and software foundations, strengthening data capabilities, and increasing strategic independence. Uncertainty acts as a catalyst for de-risking through technology, prompting companies to reinforce data infrastructure, improve data flows, secure key talent onshore, and diversify production/technology across regions to reduce concentration risk and protect profitability. This drives a fundamental shift towards more resilient and technologically advanced operating models.

viewpoints.title: Auto Ancillary Industry Entering Sustained Investment-Led Growth Phase
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings views the Indian auto ancillary industry as entering a sustained investment-led growth phase. This is driven by expanding domestic vehicle production, increasing value addition across the supply chain, and a transition towards electronics-intensive and cleaner mobility platforms. These factors are expanding the addressable market for component manufacturers and creating localization opportunities to reduce import dependence, positioning the sector for robust growth and enhanced long-term competitiveness in both domestic and export markets.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: Healthy FY27 Growth Driven by OEM Demand and Electrification Opportunities
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings anticipates the Indian auto ancillary industry to grow by 8-9% in FY27, supported by healthy OEM demand across major segments and increasing component content per vehicle. Resilient replacement demand, higher localization, and expanding global sourcing opportunities are also key drivers. The ongoing transition towards electronics-intensive and cleaner mobility platforms, specifically EV-linked components, advanced electronics, and powertrain technologies, is creating significant new opportunities. Profitability is expected to remain broadly stable, with benefits from investments materializing gradually.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: Auto Components Poised for Robust Growth and Export Surge by 2030
viewpoints.description: IBEF projects India's auto-component industry to reach US$ 200 billion by 2030, underpinned by its strong cost competitiveness, a skilled workforce, and growing domestic demand. The government's ambitious target for 30% EV market penetration by 2030 is a major catalyst, fueling demand for advanced components like batteries, power electronics, and electric drivetrains. This expansion is also expected to triple exports from US$ 20 billion to US$ 60 billion, significantly elevating India’s global automotive value chain share from 3% to 8%.

viewpoints.title: Tier 1 Suppliers Leading Tech Scale, But Need Diversification Beyond OEMs
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights Tier 1 automotive suppliers as technical scale leaders in AI, data, cyber, and simulation, exhibiting high capital efficiency. However, a strategic challenge lies in reducing dependence on OEM roadmaps, as their innovation momentum can be throttled by OEM investment timing. The report suggests that success for Tier 1s will increasingly depend on redirecting technology scale towards diversified growth, potentially through M&A for software and data capabilities, and expanding into industrial and mobility services ecosystems.

viewpoints.title: Automotive Industry Capable of Transforming Disruption into Momentum
viewpoints.description: KPMG concludes that the automotive industry, including its component suppliers, is capable of turning disruption into momentum. The sector demonstrates clear strategic conviction, increasing AI maturity, and a willingness to expand digital capabilities, despite legacy friction and coordination gaps. Success is evident in productizing platforms and scaling AI through secure operating models, achieving strong ROI and faster cycle times. The path forward emphasizes industrializing technology delivery and governance, focusing on secure data backbones and reusable architectural patterns.

viewpoints.title: Automotive Sector Demonstrates Resilience Despite Global External Shocks
viewpoints.description: CareEdge notes that bellwether industries like Automotive are reporting material improvements in corporate profitability, successfully defying tariff overhangs and global trade friction. This resilience is anchored by a sturdy Q4 GDP growth rate of 7.8%. While the immediate outlook may be flat due to ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility, the sector's ability to show material improvements against such headwinds signals a fundamental underlying strength and active strengthening of external-sector defences against recurring global instability.

demand_drivers.description: Anticipated healthy volume growth across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and two-wheelers during FY27.
Growing preference for SUVs and premium vehicles, coupled with stricter safety and emissions norms, is increasing demand for higher-value systems.
An expanding vehicle parc, rising average vehicle age, premiumisation, and increasing demand for replacement parts and regular maintenance support the aftermarket segment.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected market size of the Indian auto ancillary industry, growing from Rs 9,835 billion in FY26 to Rs 10,681 billion in FY27. Methodology encompasses healthy vehicle production, increasing component content, resilient replacement demand, higher localisation, and integration with global supply chains.
market_sizing.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

demand_drivers.description: The government's ambition for 30% EV market penetration by 2030 is fueling demand for advanced components like batteries, power electronics, and electric drivetrains.
India's competitive advantages in manufacturing and human capital drive growth.

market_sizing.methodology: Projection for the total size of India’s auto-component industry, supported by competitive advantages and demand. This includes auto component production and exports.

demand_drivers.description: Global shift towards electric vehicles creates demand for Indian-made EV components for export.
India is emerging as a global hub for auto component sourcing due to its manufacturing capabilities and cost competitiveness, leading to increased export orders.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected value of India's auto component exports, expected to triple from US$ 20 billion by 2030. This projection is also supported by a McKinsey report suggesting US$ 70-100 billion by FY30.

demand_drivers.description: India’s total vehicle parc across segments stands at roughly 333 million units and is expected to reach 430-435 million units by 2030, driving replacement demand.
Rising average age of vehicles leads to greater need for maintenance and replacement parts.

market_sizing.methodology: Projection for the domestic aftermarket auto-component market, set to grow from US$ 11.77 billion in FY25 to US$ 16 billion by 2030. This growth is driven by expanding vehicle parc and increasing vehicle age, leading to higher demand for replacement parts.

demand_drivers.description: The Indian EV market is projected to grow to US$ 191.04 billion by 2034, directly fueling demand for EV batteries.
Government schemes like PLI-ACC aim to establish domestic Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) battery manufacturing capacity, supporting market growth.

market_sizing.methodology: The Indian EV battery market is expected to expand significantly from US$ 2.71 billion in 2025 to US$ 15.90 billion by 2034. This forecast is based on the rapid growth of the electric vehicle market and increased demand for EV batteries.

demand_drivers.description: Auto component supplies to OEMs reached US$ 35.20 billion in H1 FY26, reflecting ~7% YoY growth.
The aftermarket segment was valued at US$ 6.10 billion in H1 FY26, recording ~9% growth over H1 FY25.

market_sizing.methodology: Total turnover for the automobile component industry during H1 FY26, which stood at Rs. 3,56,193 crore (US$ 41.20 billion). Domestic OEM supplies contributed ~66%, aftermarket ~11%, and exports ~23%.

pnl_drivers.description: The trade deficit reflects India's continued dependence on certain critical components such as semiconductors, battery cells, sensors, and advanced electronics.
North America accounted for 32% of FY25 exports (8.4% growth), Europe 30% (2.1% decline), and Asia 26% (15.1% robust growth).

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of trade balance for auto components in H1 FY26. Exports grew by 9.3% to US$ 12.1 billion, while imports increased by 12.5% to US$ 12.3 billion, resulting in a trade deficit of US$ 180 million. This compares to a trade surplus of US$ 150 million in H1 FY25.

new_opportunities.description: The substantial increase in investment is directed towards meeting the rising demand for electric vehicle components and expanding manufacturing capabilities.

market_sizing.methodology: ICRA estimates investment in India’s auto component industry for capacity expansion and EV parts for FY26 to be Rs. 25,000-30,000 crore (US$ 2.89-3.46 billion). This follows investments of Rs. 15,000-20,000 crore (US$ 1.73-2.31 billion) in FY25.
